example: Soft expiry 60 s, hard TTL 10 minutes: readers wait only if nobody read the key for 9 minutes.

definition: A stampede-prevention method from Vattani, Chierichetti and Lowenstein (VLDB 2015): each request refreshes a value early with a probability that rises as expiry approaches, so busy keys are usually refreshed by one request just before they expire.
example: With 5,000 requests a second, one of them almost certainly refreshes the key shortly before expiry.

definition: A leading international database research conference and its journal, Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment.
example: The XFetch paper appeared at VLDB 2015.

definition: Storing several copies of a hot key under different suffixes, such as score#0 to score#9, so reads spread over several nodes; writers must update every copy.
example: Eight copies on eight shards each take about 1/8 of the reads.

definition: A redis-cli option that scans the keyspace and reports the most frequently accessed keys; it needs an LFU maxmemory policy.
example: redis-cli --hotkeys finds the score key that is overloading one shard.

definition: One of several isolated data centres within a cloud region, with separate power and networking, so a failure in one rarely affects the others.
example: Placing Redis replicas in three availability zones survives losing one zone.

definition: Deliberately rejecting or degrading some requests when a system is overloaded, so the rest are still served instead of everything timing out.
example: Returning a cached default for non-critical reads while the database recovers is load shedding.

definition: Keeping a reduced service running when parts fail, such as showing slightly stale or simplified content instead of an error.
example: A shop shows bestsellers from yesterday when the recommendations service is down.

definition: Using several caches in layers, such as an in-process cache in front of Redis in front of the database. Each layer only sees the misses of the one above.
example: If Redis fails, the in-process layer still absorbs part of the traffic.

definition: Moving traffic to a new system in steps (say 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%), checking health at each step. A canary is the first small step.
example: A new cache cluster gets 1% of traffic first, so its misses stay within database capacity.

definition: Copying real requests to a new system without using its answers, so it warms up or is tested under realistic load before serving users.
example: Mirroring reads to a new Redis cluster fills it before the switch-over.

definition: Facebook's method for bringing a new memcache cluster online: its clients read misses from a warm cluster instead of the database. Deletes carried a two-second hold-off so a just-invalidated value was not copied over.
example: Cold cluster warm-up brought new clusters to full capacity in hours instead of days.

definition: The memcached command that stores a value only if the key does not already exist; it fails otherwise.
example: During cold cluster warm-up, a failed add told the client to read the database instead.

definition: Releasing a new version of software to servers. A deploy restarts processes, which empties in-process caches and can change cache key formats.
example: Bumping the key prefix from v2 to v3 in one deploy acts like flushing the whole cache.

definition: A configuration switch that turns a feature on or off without a new deploy. Flags must not be evicted, unlike cache entries.
example: A Redis key promo:enabled = 1 can act as a feature flag.

definition: A pause during which a language runtime stops the program to reclaim unused memory. A long pause can delay a cache write until long after the data was read.
example: A reader stalled by a 2 s GC pause writes its stale value after both deletes.

definition: A popular general-purpose programming language, used for the code examples in these lessons.
example: Python's functools.lru_cache adds an in-process LRU cache to a function.

definition: A widely used general-purpose programming language running on the Java Virtual Machine. Caffeine is a Java caching library.
example: Java's LinkedHashMap can serve as an LRU cache.

definition: A programming language from Google, popular for network services. Its singleflight package coalesces duplicate calls.
example: Go's singleflight.Group runs one load per key at a time.

definition: A personalised, frequently updated list of posts shown to a user, such as a social media timeline. Feeds are expensive to build and heavily cached.
example: Rebuilding a popular homepage feed might take 200 ms of database work.

definition: An organised, durable store of data that applications query and update, such as PostgreSQL or MySQL. In caching it is usually the slower source of truth that the cache sits in front of.
example: At a 99% hit ratio, only 1 read in 100 reaches the DB.

definition: A lightweight thread of execution managed by the Go runtime. Programs can run thousands at once, which is why Go code often needs tools such as singleflight to stop many goroutines repeating the same work.
example: 100 goroutines calling group.Do("user:42", load) together trigger one load.
